chronology: [Recap] Castakas sheltered on an extreme-gravity planet; Othon, fatally poisoned by cetacyborg gas, demands Aghnar kill him in single combat to forge a worthy avenger; Aghnar complies.
[Recap] Aghnar befriends the speaking Magon Kiowata, defeats the Magon leader, fulfills the Diamond Planet prophecy, and learns the Shabda-Oud plan to abduct Oda for her genetics.
[Recap] Aghnar captures three Shabda-Oud pilots, studies a holovid of Princess Oda, falls in love, and sets out unarmed for Amadis to join her suitors.
Aghnar arrives at Amadis disguised, concealing his Metabaron identity, and enters the courtship competition while internally suppressing violent rage at the other suitors.
Multiple suitors fail Oda's test — she demands a blue rose and rejects all substitutes, including General Amagho's grotesque offering fashioned from a defeated emperor's remains.
Aghnar manifests the true blue rose via a psychic eye-beam; Oda's father publicly names him the winner and offers the entire kingdom, but Aghnar refuses all wealth and takes only Oda.
The king orders the pair arrested; Oda holds a blade to herself and forces her father to stand down; she and Aghnar escape together.
En route to the cetacyborg, Aghnar recounts his history to Oda, recruits her as a willing ally, and plans to stage her as a bound captive to infiltrate the witches' lair.
Aghnar kills a Shabda-Oud priestess after seizing the ship's cabin, constructs a psy-cloak from her identity, and intensifies psychic mind-control over two pilots.
The group approaches the Shabda-Oud lair inside an ice asteroid; Aghnar's psy-cloak and psycho-mimetic training allow passage through the multi-layer biological and psychic identity scan.
Inside the lair, the reverend mothers receive 'captured' Oda; the eldest elder declares that Oda's womb will fulfill a twelve-generation breeding prophecy to produce Sama-Wajd.
The witches begin a forced reproductive ritual aimed at Oda, invoking Jejoh the Pure and the eventual overthrow of galactic empress Janus-Jana.
The witches' leader discovers a spy is among them and orders commands transmitted to the cetacyborg, accelerating the crisis.
Full battle erupts; Aghnar fights openly and allows the godlike entity Jejoh to bite off his arm, which is rigged with mini-bombs that detonate inside Jejoh's body.
Deprived of Jejoh's brainwave energy, the Shabda-Oud witches are catastrophically weakened and collapse as a fighting force.
The surviving elders, claiming independent power, launch a concentrated psychic assault on Aghnar; Oda merges her energy with his through a mind's-shadow union and they withstand the attack together.
Aghnar declares vengeance for Othon and Honorata achieved and expresses desire to cease being a Metabaron; a glowing cocoon-like form appears in the aftermath of the blast.
Oda survives physically but is left mentally devastated; Aghnar, one-armed, carries her toward the Metabunker while cetacyborgs block the route.
Tonto warns that only one witch remains alive and that knowledge of the cetacyborgs' secret weakness may die with her; the volume closes with a teaser for 'The Possession of Oda.'
locations: Amadis — Oda's home domain; site of the formal courtship competition and the standoff with her father
Shabda-Oud witches' lair — carved from an ice asteroid in deep space; entry controlled by a delta-psychic force-switch and multi-layer identity scans
Spacecraft used by Aghnar and Oda for travel from Amadis to the ice asteroid
The Metabunker — a facility with surgical capability; Aghnar's destination at the volume's close
Outer space — site of cetacyborg deployment, the approach to the asteroid, and the large-scale battle exterior
Diamond Planet — referenced in the Magon prophecy recap and invoked in battle dialogue
Fog World — invoked in battle dialogue as a place or faction opposed to Diamond Planet
Extreme-gravity refuge planet (prior arc) — recalled in recap; notable for giant mushrooms and floating ape communities
lore_laws: Magons are floating apes capable of speech and described as possessing a soul.
A prophecy holds that a little white Magon will lead the Magon people to the Diamond Planet.
Bio-electrograms can maintain a physically solid state only for a limited duration before dissolving.
Anti-robots are capable of rebuilding damaged robots.
The Invincible Warrior bore a scar across the right eyebrow by age 30 years, 2 months, 3 hours, 20:40:00; cause is treated as significant but remains unresolved.
Psycho-mimetics is a trainable discipline enabling a practitioner to bypass psychic or mental probes.
A delta-psychic force-switch controls entry to the Shabda-Oud asteroid lair.
Passage into the lair requires successful multi-layer biological, brainwave, and infra-conscious identity verification; a psy-cloak constructed from a killed individual can fool this system.
The Shabda-Oud witches' psychic power is entirely fueled by Jejoh's brainwaves; without Jejoh they are catastrophically weakened.
Miniaturized bombs can be concealed inside a prosthetic or armored limb and activated by contact with biological gastric fluids.
A many-headed dragon can be defeated by a single strike to its heart.
Metabaron code holds that certain trials must be faced alone.
A mind's-shadow union allows two people to merge psychic energy in a state described as permanent.
Sama-Wajd is the prophesied chosen hermaphrodite expected to dethrone Janus-Jana, empress of the galaxy; the Shabda-Oud have pursued the genetic conditions for this birth across twelve generations.
Cetacyborgs are creatures created by the Shabda-Oud witches; knowledge of their vulnerability is held only by the witches.
The Metabunker contains surgical and medical capability, and Tonto is able to perform operations there.
Janus-Jana is identified as the current empress of the galaxy and the target of the Shabda-Oud succession plot.
major_events: Othon's death: Aghnar kills his father in sanctioned single combat, framing Othon's sacrifice as the act that shapes Aghnar into an avenger capable of defeating the Shabda-Oud.
The courtship of Oda at Amadis: Aghnar wins the blue-rose trial, rejects the offered kingdom, and escapes with Oda after her father's armed standoff is broken by Oda's suicide threat.
Infiltration of the ice asteroid lair: Aghnar disguises himself via a murdered priestess's psy-cloak and passes multi-layer psychic security scans to deliver Oda to the witches as a deliberate trap.
The Shabda-Oud ritual: the witches restrain Oda in a forced reproductive ceremony intended to produce Sama-Wajd, the prophesied hermaphrodite destined to dethrone empress Janus-Jana.
Destruction of Jejoh: Aghnar sacrifices his own arm — loaded with mini-bombs — by provoking Jejoh to consume it; the bombs detonate in Jejoh's stomach, destroying the witches' central power source.

The Elders' psychic assault and the mind's-shadow union: the surviving elders spend their remaining power in a direct mental attack; Aghnar and Oda survive only by merging their psychic energy permanently.
Vengeance declared: Aghnar states that Othon and Honorata have been avenged and that he wishes to end his Metabaron role; a glowing cocoon-like object appears in the aftermath.

Oda gravely wounded: the battle leaves Oda's mind devastated; Aghnar must fight through a cetacyborg blockade to reach the Metabunker, and Tonto warns the last witch — the only source of the cetacyborgs' weakness — may soon be dead.
open_uncertainties: Whether Aghnar can fight through the cetacyborg blockade and reach the Metabunker before Oda's mental condition becomes irreversible.
Whether Oda will recover from her psychic devastation; at the volume's end she is described as physically alive but mentally destroyed.
Whether the last surviving Shabda-Oud witch will be found in time for her knowledge of the cetacyborgs' secret weakness to be extracted.
The nature and origin of the glowing cocoon or egg-like form that appeared in the chamber after the final energy blast — not explained within this volume.
Whether Aghnar will successfully renounce the Metabaron identity as he declares, or be forced to continue; the next episode title 'The Possession of Oda' implies the crisis deepens.
The cause of the Invincible Warrior's eyebrow scar, explicitly deferred in Tonto's frame sequences and never revealed in this volume.
The long-term consequences of the mind's-shadow union between Aghnar and Oda, described only as making them 'united forever.'
Whether the Shabda-Oud breeding plan to produce Sama-Wajd was definitively thwarted by Jejoh's destruction or merely interrupted.
recurring_motifs: The blue rose as emblem of authentic spiritual connection, contrasted against hollow displays of wealth, military conquest, and theatrical gifts from suitors.
Sacrificial mutilation as tactical weapon: Aghnar's severed arm functions as an internal bomb, continuing the lineage's pattern of bodies weaponized through deliberate loss.

Psychic and mental warfare: identity scans, psy-cloaks, psycho-mimetic bypass training, mind-control over pilots, and the Elders' final collective assault all treat cognition as a primary battlefield.
Hereditary destiny versus personal will: Aghnar repeatedly declares intent to abandon the Metabaron succession while simultaneously executing the most Metabaron-defining acts of the arc.
Deception and disguise as survival: Aghnar hides his identity at Amadis then disguises himself as a witches' priestess, both subterfuges serving the same revenge arc.
Forced reproduction and lineage as power: the Shabda-Oud's entire operation centers on controlling whose genes produce the next prophesied being, echoing the broader Metabaron dynastic theme.

The frame narrative of robots recounting history to Lothar: Tonto and another robot bicker while narrating the saga, deferring and teasing unresolved mysteries such as the Invincible Warrior's eyebrow scar.
Aghnar's arc toward a peaceful ordinary family life with Oda, invoked multiple times but blocked at every turn by duty, battle, and catastrophic injury.
title: The Lair of the Shabda-Oud
